newsitem.title: COLOMBIA: Colombia shares mixed, Bancoquia soars.
newsitem.headline: Colombia shares mixed, Bancoquia soars.

text.p: Colombian stocks ended mixed in active trading that saw Bancoquia lead gainers for the second consecutive trading session.
The bank, Colombia's eighth largest in terms of assets, is the target of an expected takeover by Spain's Banco Santander .

Medellin's IBOMED general price index fell 0.52 points to close at to close at 16,732.04 on a trading volume of just over 1 billion pesos. Bogota's IBB ended up 0.42 percent, meanwhile, ending at 1,068.37 on above-average volume of 2.36 billion pesos.
Brokers said trading was partly fueled by a cut in central bank inerest rates Friday that could take some of the premium off the fixed-income market.
"Clients whose fixed-income obligations matured today began buying those stocks that are still cheap," said one Bogota-based broker.

Bancoquia, which closed up 3.53 percent in Bogota Friday at 3,101 pesos per share, jumped an additional 6.61 percent in the capital Monday to close at 3,306 pesos a share. It matched the same 6.61 percent in Medellin, where it ended the day at 3,305 pesos.
"People are holding on to Bancoquia and are reluctant to sell the stock, unless it's at a high price," said one broker, adding, "There's a lot of speculation surrounding the bank's shares."

Traders have speculated that Bancoquia may be sold at 4,500 pesos a shares, but that figure remains guesswork and could be significantly different depending on the number of shares bought and whether the bank issues new stock.

Santander is expected to buy a 55 percent stake in Bancoquia later this year. There are widespread expectations that Santander's investment in the bank, initially valued at $151 million, will have a positive effect on net income.
Other gainers Monday included Banco de Colombia, which rose 0.95 percent to close at 422 pesos a share in Bogota.
"Banco de Colombia continues at an attractive price for long-term investment and the rating agency forecasts are good," a trader said.
